the columns in their given order
the cells strong: a heatmap, whose colour is the message: the steps at full strength (owner, 1 Oct 2026)
the cells: a sequential palette; no dividing value the audience sees: one ramp, darker meaning more, never diverging about the middle of the data (G4.10, D-37 (a))
the cells: the values are fairly even (the fullest of seven equal steps would hold 21 % of them): equal steps on rounded values, the most honest cut
a key: a bar of the 6 classes, “Customer satisfaction (on 10)” above it, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 under it, above the grid at its right (G5.13, s. 0204)
the lightest step #dceaf6: OKLab ΔE 0.073 from the page and 0.206 from the missing grey; the breaks in the key rounded and formatted as a set
the cells coloured in classes, sequential, equal steps: 4–5 | 5–6 | 6–7 | 7–8 | 8–9 | 9–10, darker meaning further from the lowest (G4.14)

findings.message: chart.value_labels off departs from the procedure, which gives on (every value fits its cell: the numbers carry the values exactly and the colour shows the pattern (G7.36))
findings.reason: where each store stands against 7 is the message, read from the colours against their key; the scores themselves are not
findings.title: fewer values than scale labels: label the values directly

source.shows: a diverging ramp whose dividing value is the audience's, 7 on a 10-point rating, not the middle of the scale (R3-13, G4.11): two ramps meeting at a light grey at 7, intensity growing with the distance from it, symmetric about 7 and cut at the scale's maximum, so that the key's tick at 7 stands right of its middle (R3-14, R4-9); the values left out so that the key is read (a guided departure, with its reason); red below 7 and green above (D-18); synthetic ratings (the book shows only keys)
